title: aidd retired names
description: The format of schemas/retired-names.json: the names aidd retired, and what replaced each. A row says where a name stood (`surface` and `old`), what it became (`new`, null for a cut), and how `aidd upgrade` moves it (`rule`). `aidd upgrade --yes` moves every file in an old shape to today's, and the loaders name the row when they meet an old name. A rename, a cut, or a move of a name a person writes adds a row here and no code.

retired.description: One row for each retired name, by surface in the order the `surface` enum lists them, then by `old`.

path.description: A path into a file's YAML or JSON: keys joined by dots. `name[]` is each item of the list at `name`, and `*` is any key of the mapping. For a `cli_value` row, a flag and its value as a person types them, such as `--change-type infra`. For a `standard_id` row, a library standard's id.

id.description: The row's name, unique in the file. A `value` rule is the function in `aidd.setup.migrating` that has this id.

surface.description: Where the name stood: `config` is `.aidd/config.yaml` and the parents it extends from the repository, `spec`, `intent`, `proposal`, `runbook`, `postmortem`, and `exploration` are the front matter of a work item or a typed document, `handoff` is an `aidd-handoff` block in a Spec, `standard` is the front matter of an edited copy of a library standard, `sitemap` is the product prototype's `<docs>/design/app/sitemap.json`, a JSON file, `record` is a record file in `.git/aidd/records/`, which aidd never rewrites, `cli_flag` is a flag of an `aidd` command, which no file holds and no upgrade moves, so the command that meets the old flag names its replacement, `cli_value` is a value a person types after a flag of the CLI or gives to the MCP tool of the same name, and `standard_id` is the id of a library standard that a project copied.

old.description: The retired name, as a path.

new.description: What replaced it, as a path, or null when nothing did. A `rename` keeps the parent and changes the last key.

retired_in.description: The aidd version that stopped reading the old name.

rule.description: How `aidd upgrade` moves it. `rename` changes the last key and keeps its value, its place, and its comment. `cut` removes the key, with a line that shows its value. `value` runs the function with this row's `id`, for a change that moves a value to another place or another file, or changes the value itself, such as to its opposite. A `value` row that changes only values names its key as both `old` and `new`. `read_both` is for a record, which aidd never rewrites: a reader reads the old name, or each old value in `read_as`, as the new one. `manual` is for a value a person types, which no file holds: the CLI refuses it and names `new`, what to type now.

read_as.description: Only with `read_both`, for a retired value: each old value of the key `old` names, and the value a reader reads it as. The writer never writes an old value.

note.description: Why it was retired and where its fact lives now. A cut prints it, and a loader adds it to the error for the old name.
